Thanks Rafael. Quick product clarifications so we don't overpromise to Keystone:

- Hosted API: we offer customer encryption-in-transit and at-rest; BYOK is not available for hosted tenants today — we provide per-tenant encryption keys managed by Redwood, plus exportable audit logs.
- Dedicated / Private: BYOK (customer KMS) is supported in Private deployments and in Dedicated Reserved when the customer requests an HSM/KMS integration; this is an engineering enablement and requires an onboarding window.

For Keystone's ask, we should scope three deliverables:
1) One-page BYOK handshake diagram and high-level SOC2-compatible description (can go to Keystone legal).
2) 30-day redacted audit log sample (events + timestamps; strip any PII).
3) SSO fallback emergency access plan (short runbook and who to contact).

Irene — can Security draft #1 and #2, or should we route engineering to generate the log sample? If we need a switchover test for fallback access, that may require a short runbook review with Ops.

I'll draft the product caveats (Hosted vs Private) and propose language that aligns with our existing SLAs.

-Marissa
Sr. PM, Platform

We can produce a minimal evidence pack but need to lock scope. Internal checklist and quick notes: 

- Audit logs: we have the ingestion pipeline that can export ndjson samples. Ops can produce a 30-day window from staging/dedicated nodes; will redact user identifiers per our redaction script. ETA: May 9 if we get approval.
- BYOK diagram: I will produce a one-pager that shows KMS handshake on Private (customer KMS -> HSM -> runtime) and note limitations for Hosted tenants.
- SSO fallback: security policy allows an emergency access flow that uses a short-lived admin token + documented approvals; however, for Keystone we should propose a role-based emergency Break-Glass process that requires two approvers from Keystone and one Redwood approver.

Open questions for Product / Infra: 
- Jonas: will Infra require an engineer to run the log export (time/cost)?
- Marissa: language around "emergency access" needs to be narrow — we should avoid implying broad console access.

I will attach the draft BYOK diagram and an outline of the evidence pack by EOD May 4.

Irene Choi
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: draft_byo_diagram.svg (will attach in follow-up)

Ops update on feasibility:

- Log export: we can produce a redacted 30-day ndjson sample from dedicated staging within 48 hours of sign-off (Irene and Rafael to confirm what fields to redact). The export job will run on infra during a maintenance window; low risk.
- BYOK artifacts: diagram is product/security owned. For Private deploys we can demo key handshake in our staging cluster; producing an artifact (diagram + sequence) is ~2 days of work between Security and Infra.
- SSO fallback: we have an existing break-glass capability used for critical incidents. To generate an official runbook and the required approval template for Keystone will take ~3 business days to finalize.

- May 4: Irene shares draft diagram + redaction spec.
- May 5-6: Infra runs log export, redact, and hand to Security.
